# glinet_client_block (Resource)

Blocks a client by its MAC address: the MAC address is an entry in the block list of the router (`black_white_list`). The router has one block list for all clients, and uses it only in block-list mode. The resource does not manage the access control mode (see `glinet_access_control`): create and destroy fail when the router is not in block-list mode, because it is not known what a write to the block list does in allow-list mode. While the router is not in block-list mode, refresh keeps the resource in the state and shows a warning. The provider writes the MAC address in upper case, as the web UI does, and finds entries without letter case. The state keeps `mac` in the letter case of the configuration. Import sets `mac` in lower case. Destroy removes the MAC address in each letter case. It was not verified that the router blocks the traffic of a client in the list.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_client_block" "tablet" {
  mac = "02:00:00:00:00:01"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mac` (String) MAC address of the client, in lower case or upper case, for example `02:00:00:00:00:01`. A change of only the letter case changes only the state. Another change replaces the resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the MAC address, in lower or upper case.
terraform import glinet_client_block.tablet 02:00:00:00:00:01
```
